hypothesis: FORCING: the author constrained the CIPHERTEXT so that a ciphertext-visible positional subset (line initials, page initials, word initials, or their finals) spells or encodes something. Detectable with no key at all. Motivated by round17/D-01, which proved the anti-repeat filter is machine-applied, i.e. the author demonstrably wrote a rejection sampler that enforces a ciphertext-level predicate; forcing is the hypothesis that the sampler enforced a second one.
raw_status: negative-for-forcing (one pre-registered test fired and was traced to a typographic confound)
threshold: inherited hard gate p < 0.001 (campaign14/REDTEAM-PROPOSALS.md), Bonferroni-corrected over the 21 pre-registered tests to alpha_test = 4.762e-5
control_detail: Synthetic 12,956-rune streams with LP2's exact separator pattern and page geometry, drawn from the fitted H0 generator (uniform runes under a memoryless lag-1 anti-repeat rejection filter at s=0.8075) and laid out by the SAME greedy line-breaker with the SAME fitted glyph widths, so the control carries the real book's inspection-paradox size bias rather than a straw null. Generator validated before use: doublet rate 0.006719 +/- 0.000614 vs LP2's 0.006638; IoC*N 0.99991 vs 1.000. Corroboration: the layout-aware null built on purely synthetic forcing-free streams has mean 64.68 sd 14.62, matching the null built by reflowing the real shuffled ciphertext (65.60, sd 14.48). A fraction f of the 594 line initials was then forced to a fixed 594-rune phrase under BOTH mechanisms (M1 assign-unconditionally; M2 filter-wins), 200 replicates per cell, 2,000 null streams for the critical values. MEASURED POWER at alpha_test=4.762e-5: the layout-corrected detector D_layout has false-positive rate 0.000/200 at f=0 and power 1.000 at f>=0.60 under both mechanisms (f80 = 0.60), collapsing to 0.595/0.460 at f=0.40 and 0.045/0.060 at f=0.30. Arm C's D_C1 reaches 0.765 at f=1.00 under M1 and 0.000 at EVERY f under M2. Arm B's planted-English acrostic control recovered at -4.372 against a bar of -6.806. CRITICAL NEGATIVE CONTROL RESULT: the detector C-02 literally specified -- the same chi-square judged against a FLAT null -- has a measured false-positive rate of 0.490 at f=0, i.e. it fires on forcing-free LP2-like data half the time, against a nominal 4.8e-5. Its power is also non-monotone (0.490 at f=0, ~0.30 at f=0.05-0.10). The literal C-02 detector is not usable on this object; only the layout-corrected one is, and the negative reported here is the layout-corrected one's.
null: Arm A: exact multivariate-hypergeometric size-matched resampling of positions from the ciphertext's own urn (200,000 draws, resolution floor 5.0e-6), plus a layout-aware null that reflows shuffled text through the fitted greedy line-breaker. Arm B: max-statistic null over the identical 232-variant Gematria-Primus sweep applied to size-matched draws from the ciphertext, Gumbel-fitted to the pre-registered alpha. Arm C: allocation null over doublet counts preserving the measured anti-repeat suppression, plus a constrained permutation null for the difference channel.
result: ONE pre-registered test fired and it is typographic, not cryptographic. A1 (line-initial runes, n=594): chi2(28)=78.656, empirical p<=5.0e-6, asymptotic p=1.06e-6 -- clears the gate by two orders of magnitude and exceeds all 200,000 flat-null draws (max 74.04). Post-hoc confound analysis identifies the cause as the inspection paradox under a greedy width-based line-breaker: the rune straddling the right margin is length-biased into the next line's first slot, so P(rune r begins a line) ~ p(r)*width(r). Rune widths recovered by least squares from the 539 width-limited lines correlate at +0.879 with BabelStone Runic advance widths (external, independent of the ciphertext); they correlate at +0.697 with the line-initial log excess; they drop the statistic to 38.73 (p~0.085) and, cross-validated on held-out lines, to 31.04 (p~0.32); and a reflow null built from them (53.5% exact line-length reproduction, 82.5% within +/-1 rune) has mean 65.60 vs the observed 78.66, giving p_layout=0.177. All other 20 pre-registered tests NEGATIVE, including page-initial (p=0.387), word-initial (p=0.706), all six Arm B message families, and every Arm C position-conditioned filter statistic.
coverage: 12,956 runes / 55 pages / 594 lines / 2,928 words / 219 sentence units, pages 0-54 only. Arm A: 10 positional subsets (line/word/page/sentence initials and finals plus two adjacency controls), chi-square vs both the full-text distribution and flat uniform, 200,000 exact size-matched draws each. Arm B: 6 families x 232 Gematria-Primus variants per read (forward/reverse x identity/Atbash x 29 Caesar shifts x keep/drop-F), covering the 594-rune line-initial sequence, 55 per-page acrostics, 108 per-page main and anti diagonals, 77 every-Nth-line-initial subsequences for N=2..12 at all phases, the 55-rune page-initial and page-final strings, and the 2,928-rune word-initial and word-final strings; max-statistic nulls with the identical sweep. Arm C: doublet residual rate and 29-bin difference channel conditioned on position-within-line and position-within-word, suppression estimates with Wilson intervals, and the mutual information between each line-final rune and the next line-initial rune. Durable by-products: a 29-rune glyph-width table recovered from the transcription and externally validated against a real runic font, and a validated greedy line-breaker model of the book's typesetting. Measured sensitivity floor: forcing of >=60% of the 594 line initials would have been detected with probability 1.000; below f~0.40 the corrected detector is largely blind and at f<=0.20 it is blind.
not_covered: (1) Arm C is badly underpowered in the deficit direction: with only 539 line-boundary transitions at a ~0.7% residual rate it can detect a boundary suppression only at s <= -0.712 (a 71% EXCESS of boundary doublets) at the pre-registered alpha, and CANNOT detect a deficit at any alpha, not even a total ban on boundary doublets. A forcing scheme whose conflicts were resolved by re-rolling is therefore invisible to Arm C at this sample size. (2) Arm A's layout correction now sets the sensitivity floor for line-initial forcing: because typography already lifts the line-initial chi-square to a null mean of 65.6, weak forcing is masked -- see the measured f80 in RESULTS.md section 5 for the exact fraction of lines that would have to be forced. (3) Not tested: forcing on subsets this lane did not enumerate (column-wise readings across pages, ornament-relative positions, per-page rune-index arithmetic, positions defined by the 47 catalogued ornament bands -- that is lane L3's ground); forcing of a NON-rune-valued feature (word lengths, line lengths, punctuation placement) rather than of rune identity; and forcing detectable only jointly with a key hypothesis. (4) Arm B scored English only; a forced acrostic in a non-English language, in digits, or in prime values would not have been seen by the quadgram scorer -- this is the same English-only scorer limitation lane L7 is auditing. (5) The whole lane rests on the krisyotam transcription's LINE BREAKS being the book's real line breaks; a from-scratch re-read (PARKED.md, per-rune vision) would independently confirm both the geometry and the glyph-width table.
reproduce: cd liber-primus/analysis/round18/L4-forcing && python3 parse_structure.py && python3 armA_uniformity.py 200000 && python3 confound_layout.py 5000 && python3 armC_rejection.py 200000 && python3 armB_message.py 1000 && python3 control_power.py
reopens_if: (a) a re-transcription changes the line breaks or the 86/4 doublet counts, since the whole layout correction is conditioned on them; (b) anyone measures real glyph widths from the 400-DPI page renders and they disagree with the fitted table (corr +0.879 with BabelStone is supportive, not decisive -- the book's own font was not identified); (c) a scorer that is not English-only, or a non-rune-valued feature channel (word lengths, line lengths, punctuation), is applied to the same positional subsets; (d) lane L3's ornament catalogue yields positional subsets this lane did not enumerate; (e) sample size at line boundaries can be raised -- e.g. by pooling LP1's runic pages -- which is the only way to lift Arm C out of its deficit-direction blind spot.
notes: Two instrument findings are worth more than the verdict. FIRST: a flat null is WRONG for any line-position statistic on LP2. Typography alone lifts the line-initial chi-square from a flat-null mean of 26.9 to 65.6, so a flat null manufactures p ~ 1e-6 out of a greedy line-breaker. Any future acrostic or positional attack must use the layout-aware null in confound_layout.py. SECOND, and recorded per Round 18 rule 2: this lane's own first draft of Arm C used a permutation null that reshuffled line-initial runes among themselves, which destroys the anti-repeat filter -- a property established at >=0.99 power by round17/D-01 and therefore part of H0, not something to randomise away. The tell was C1 returning p = 1.00000 and C4 returning a null mean of 83.7 against 27 df. Both were rebuilt (allocation null preserving the measured suppression; difference channel restricted to bins 1-28) before any verdict was taken. A null that destroys a known H0 property cannot test anything -- it only measures how strongly H0 holds.
